title: This Inch-Long Sea Slug Steals Venom From Deadly Jellyfish
subject: blue dragon sea slug

scenes.text: This slug is only an inch long. Its sting can be worse than a man o' war's.
It's the blue dragon. It floats upside down on the sea surface, held up by a gas bubble in its stomach.
It can't make venom. So it hunts animals that can, like the Portuguese man o' war.
It eats the prey but doesn't digest the stinging cells. They move into its feathery arms.
scenes.keywords: blue dragon sea slug close up

scenes.text: There they wait, stored and ready, to fire if anything touches it.
So the sting that hurts you isn't the slug's. It was stolen.

description:
The blue dragon sea slug grows to about 3 centimeters and cannot make venom of its own.
It eats Portuguese man o' war and keeps their stinging cells, stored in its feathery arms, for its own defense. Some reports say the sting can be worse than a man o' war's.
Would you pick one up?
first_comment: Would you pick up a blue dragon on the beach? Be honest.
